 Optimizely reports 'security incident' that involved malware in customers' digital products 
 Some Optimizely customers said they are aware of the reported incident. 
 By Max Zahn November 17, 2026, 2:12 PM 
 1:22 Stock Photo/Getty Images Optimizely, a platform for digital tools used by Zoom and a host of other companies, said it has experienced a "security incident" that planted malware in at least some of its clients' digital infrastructure.
 "Optimizely identified a security incident in which an unauthorized party exploited a vulnerability," the company said, noting the intruder had used the vulnerability to "add malicious JavaScript to some customer projects."
 Related Trump Asia trip live updates: Trump and Quad leaders gather in Manila Some Optimizely customers, including Zoom, issued statements on Tuesday saying they are aware of the reported incident.
 "As a precautionary measure, Zoom has disabled Optimizely across our production environments. At this time, we have not identified any impact to customer data. We continue to monitor the situation closely," the videoconferencing company said .
 STOCK PHOTO/Adobe Stock In a statement to ABC News, furniture giant IKEA said: “We are aware of reports concerning a security issue involving a third-party website service provider that may have affected a number of organisations, including IKEA."

 "We are investigating the matter to understand any potential impact on our digital services and customers. Protecting customer information and maintaining the security of our services remain a top priority," the statement added.
 In its latest update, Optimizely said: "For the US region, recommendations continue to be served, and they are being refreshed with the latest data, so quality should return to normal over the course of today."
